## Summary
A report run of `aaif-sync chapters organizers` took about 50 minutes. The time didn't go into new work: each step is a separate process, and each one asked Slack and Google the same questions the previous step had just asked. This PR gives each run two memo files, deleted when the run ends, and adds a thread pool to `sync_crm`. Measured 2026-09-22, the same run takes about 11 minutes and every step still reports `in sync`. A full 18-step report run takes about 21 minutes of step time.

## Changesets

### 1. `perf(sync): ask Slack and Google each question once per run`
**Files:** `lib/aaif_events/{slack,gws,jsoncache}.py`, `skills/aaif-sync/scripts/sync.py`, `skills/aaif-sync/SKILL.md`, and tests
- `AAIF_SLACK_RUN_MEMO` covers `users.lookupByEmail` and `users.info`. Five steps used to resolve the same ~180 organizers at about 1.5s a call.
- `AAIF_GWS_RUN_MEMO` covers Sheets and Drive reads, **in report runs only**. A run that asked for `--write` gets no read memo for any of its steps, because a later step must see an earlier step's write. For example, `luma` reads the Chapters List after `chapters` and `resources` have written it. Downloads (`--output`, or `alt` in the params) always go to Google.
- Both memos use a single `jsoncache.RunMemo`: append-only, 0600 from creation, a torn line counts as a miss, and access is locked for thread pools.
- `sync.py` stays lib-free. `test_sync.py` checks that the runner's variable names match the lib's.

### 2. `perf(crm): open chapter workbooks in a pool of six`
**Files:** `skills/aaif-sync-organizers/scripts/sync_crm.py`
`sync_crm` made two Drive calls per chapter, about 0.75s each, one chapter after another. The reads now go through a six-worker pool, as in `sync_about`. Planning stays sequential and in folder order. The download path now includes the folder id, so two city names that sanitise to the same string can't collide.

### 3. `fix(sync): address self-review findings on the run memos`
**Files:** the lib memo modules, `sync.py`, `SKILL.md`, and tests (new `lib/aaif_events/tests/test_run_memo.py`)
- **The memo files are deleted when the run ends**, including after a crash or interrupt. They hold whole intake tabs and Slack profiles, more than any report keeps.
- The gws memo keeps only a well-formed answer (a JSON object with no `error` key). The Slack memo keeps only accounts that were found. It never keeps a failed call, a "no such user", or channel membership.
- `RunMemo` returns a fresh copy on every hit, handles short writes, and treats a failed write as "not memoised".
- Comments corrected, and test gaps filled (see the review comments).

## What gets remembered, and for how long
| | Slack memo | Google memo |
|---|---|---|
| Report run | found accounts | reads that parsed as an answer |
| `--write` run | found accounts | **none** |
| Standalone engine run | none | none |
| After the run | deleted | deleted |

## Not done, on purpose
- **Using the read memo under `--write` (clearing it on each write)** was suggested in review. It was skipped because several engines write through their own `gws` or Slack wrappers, and those would never clear the memo, so a later step could still read data from before a write. Report-only is the rule that can't serve stale data.

## Test Plan
- [x] `PYTHONPATH=lib python -m pytest lib/aaif_events/tests -q`: 514 passed
- [x] Every skill test script under aaif-sync, aaif-sync-organizers, aaif-sync-slack, aaif-audit-slack and aaif-sync-chapters passes
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` and every `scripts/check_*.py` guard pass
- [x] Live report runs: `chapters organizers` took about 50 minutes before and about 11 after, with identical outcomes. The full 18-step run took about 21 minutes of step time. After the review fixes, a live `chapters` run was in sync and left no memo file behind.
- [ ] A `--write` run confirms that no `gws-memo.jsonl` appears in its run directory
